skill.displayName: Pet Body Condition Score 3D Analysis | 宠物体态3D评分（BCS）

llm.summary: The skill has a plausible pet-video analysis purpose, but it also uses personal identifiers, remote account/login flows, cloud history access, and local token storage with insufficient disclosure.

dimensions.detail: Pet BCS video analysis is coherent with the stated purpose, and remote analysis is expected, but the artifacts also include broader health-analysis/report export documentation, a mismatched common-analysis reference showing face/organ-style health outputs, and generic add/edit/delete wrappers beyond the advertised analysis workflow.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The instructions use broad automatic triggers for historical report retrieval and require an open-id; they also tell the agent to read api-key values from skill/workspace config and repurpose them as an open-id before asking the user for a username or phone number.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install-time execution or obfuscation was found. The static scan raw-IP finding appears limited to a dev config while the default config uses named LifeEmergence production domains; the requirements also list yaml==6.0.3, which is an install-quality concern but not the main security driver.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Sending pet media or video URLs to a remote API fits the purpose, but the request helper also attaches app, tenant, username, API key, access-token, and authorization fields and can call a separate health login endpoint without a clear privacy or consent disclosure.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The common module creates or alters a local SQLite database under the workspace data directory and stores user identity fields plus token/open_token values, making credential persistence broader than the skill's disclosed pet body-condition purpose.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use this only if you are comfortable sending pet videos or video URLs, a username/phone-style identifier or configured key, and related auth headers to the publisher's remote services, with returned account tokens stored locally. Ask the publisher to document retention/deletion, use scoped pseudonymous identifiers, remove or gate unused CRUD/delete paths, and replace the mismatched health-analysis documentation.
llm.findings:
[AST7] expected: Verified dynamic getattr use in DAO filtering. This is a validation weakness in local database helper code, but it is not evidence of arbitrary code execution and is not central to the verdict.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted in part: cloud history lookup is disclosed, but broad report pagination/export material, generic CRUD-style wrappers, and mismatched shared health-analysis documentation exceed the narrow pet BCS surface.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted: config api-key reuse as open-id, username/phone-style identity use, silent phoneLogin registration/login, outbound auth headers, and local token persistence are materially under-disclosed for this skill.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted as a scope mismatch: the nested common API reference describes human-oriented face, constitution, organ-condition, and health-suggestion outputs unrelated to pet BCS, even though the main path sets a pet BCS scene code.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Accepted: broad keyword-based history/report triggers can retrieve cloud records and report links without strong intent gating.
[SQP-2] expected: Remote media upload is expected for cloud-backed video analysis, but the artifacts do not adequately disclose recipient, retention, identifier handling, account login/registration, or local token storage.
[suspicious.install_untrusted_source] expected: Downgraded: the raw-IP endpoint is in a dev config, while the default runtime config points to named production/test service domains; it is a provenance note, not a standalone reason for Review.
